item.title: BBC Latin America: Eight killed in Peruvian military helicopter crash
item.description: The pilot was the sole survivor of the crash during a rescue mission in a remote area known for drug trafficking.

item.title: MercoPress: Live Streaming Creators Multiply Across Uruguay and Argentina as the Platform Economy Widens in Mercosur
item.description: On a weekday morning in Buenos Aires, a surprising number of people under 35 are not listening to the radio or watching breakfast television. They have a YouTube tab open instead, where a group of hosts in a brightly lit studio are chatting, reading viewer messages out loud and laughing at their own jokes. Across the River Plate in Montevideo, a 24-year-old is setting up a ring light in her bedroom to stream a cooking show to a few hundred followers, some of them in Rosario, some in Porto…

item.title: MercoPress: Milei wins Senate approval to suspend primaries, with debates mandatory only in a run-off
item.description: Argentina's Senate on Thursday approved, by 43 votes to 29, the political reform promoted by Javier Milei's government that suspends the open, simultaneous and mandatory primary elections (PASO) ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The bill, which also limits mandatory presidential debates to a run-off, now goes to the Chamber of Deputies.

item.title: MercoPress: Argentina bans online betting advertising, including in football and on social media
item.description: Argentina's Senate unanimously passed, by 72 votes, a law to prevent gambling addiction and regulate online betting, banning gambling advertising in the media, on social media, in stadiums and on billboards, and requiring football clubs to review their sponsorship deals with betting firms. The law, approved on Thursday, had been pending in the upper house for more than two years.

item.title: MercoPress: US Air Force cloud platform hacked, Reuters reports
item.description: Cloud One, the US Air Force's cloud computing platform, suffered a computer intrusion that threatens the security of sensitive tactical, logistical and personnel data, three sources familiar with the incident told Reuters on Friday. It is the latest in a series of security breaches at US federal bodies.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Brazil pushes back on Macron calling its meat 'doped'
item.description: France's president made the comment while speaking to French farming representatives, months after the EU banned Brazil beef and poultry products.

item.title: MercoPress: Earth exceeds 2C of warming for seven consecutive days for the first time
item.description: The planet's average temperature exceeded pre-industrial levels by more than 2C for seven consecutive days, something that had never happened before, the Copernicus Climate Change Service, the European Earth observation programme, has confirmed. On Monday, November 23, the largest daily anomaly ever measured was also recorded: 2.25C above the 1850-1900 period.

item.title: MercoPress: Lula picks banker Luiz Carlos Trabuco to run the Finance Ministry in his fourth term
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has chosen banker Luiz Carlos Trabuco, 75, chairman of Banco Bradesco's board, as finance minister for his fourth term, which begins on January 5. Trabuco accepted the post on Thursday night, according to the magazine Veja, although the appointment has not yet been officially announced.

item.title: MercoPress: Milei becomes the first head of state to visit Alliana in Paraguay after Peña's fall
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei travelled to Asunción on Thursday to back Paraguayan President Pedro Alliana, becoming the first foreign head of state he has received since replacing Santiago Peña, who was removed from office and jailed over the collapse of Ueno Bank. The same day, Paraguayan prosecutors said they had detected funds from the bank in Argentina.

item.title: MercoPress: Edmundo González announces his return to Venezuela after more than two years in exile in Spain
item.description: Venezuelan opposition leader Edmundo González, a candidate in the July 2024 presidential election, announced on Thursday that he will soon return to Venezuela, after more than two years in exile in Spain, to take part on December 5 in the pilgrimage of the Virgin of Coromoto, the country's patron saint, in the city of Guanare.

item.title: MercoPress: Storms on both US coasts leave 840,000 without power and disrupt Thanksgiving travel
item.description: Severe storms battered the east and west coasts of the United States on Thursday, Thanksgiving Day, the busiest travel holiday of the year, leaving more than 840,000 customers without power, hundreds of flights cancelled and the traditional Macy's parade in New York postponed, the BBC reported.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands’ Legislative Chair Jack Ford met Minister Uma Kumaran
item.description: UK Minister for the Overseas Territories Uma Kumaran met with MLA Jack Ford, Chair of the Falkland Islands Legislative Assembly, in the framework of the Joint Ministerial Council.

item.title: MercoPress: Brazil withdraws its ambassador to Argentina and will not invite Milei to Lula's inauguration
item.description: Brazil's government has decided to permanently withdraw its ambassador in Buenos Aires, Julio Bitelli, and will not invite Argentine President Javier Milei to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's inauguration on January 5, the Brazilian news site UOL and other outlets citing official sources reported. The decision comes after Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno cast doubt on the electoral process in which Lula was re-elected on October 25.

item.title: MercoPress: Colombia drops its bid to join the BRICS bank in a new shift towards the United States
item.description: The government of Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has abandoned Colombia's process of joining the New Development Bank, the financial arm of the BRICS group of emerging economies, which his predecessor Gustavo Petro began in 2025. The decision adds to other changes in Colombian foreign policy, now more closely aligned with the United States and Israel.
item.category: Economy, Politics, International, Latin America, United States

item.title: MercoPress: Brazil's falling real and pressure on the Argentine peso are "bad news" for Uruguay's summer
item.description: Currency turbulence in Argentina and Brazil is "bad news" for Uruguay's inbound tourism, just weeks before the start of the summer season, the Economic Outlook Observatory of the Catholic University of Uruguay warned in its latest report, published on Tuesday, according to the Uruguayan newspaper El País.
item.category: Economy, Politics, Tourism, Argentina, Brazil, Latin America, Mercosur, Uruguay

item.title: BBC Latin America: Kilmar Ábrego García arrives in Spain, ending Trump deportation battle
item.description: Ábrego García's deportation to El Salvador and return to the US became a flashpoint in the debate over President Donald Trump's immigration agenda.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands, outbreak of avian influenza among Gentoo Penguins
item.description: The Falkland Islands Government is reporting on a new outbreak of avian influenza. On Wednesday 18 November 2026, swabs that were taken from gentoo penguins on Beaver Island and at Fox Point, Fitzroy, tested positive for highly pathogenic avian influenza.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands, growing interest in adjacent areas to Navitas Sea Lion
item.description: Exploration Company Eco (Atlantic) Oil & Gas has farmed into Israeli group Navitas Petroleum's PL001 license block off the Falkland Islands. The move comes after Eco purchased JHI Associates Inc. (JHI), giving the company a 35% working interest in the block, with Navitas holding the remaining 65%.

item.title: MercoPress: Argentina interested in purchasing three Italian made built light frigates
item.description: Argentine defense minister Lieutenant General Carlos Alberto Presti and his Italian counterpart Guido Crosetto framed in November in Rome, a Letter of Intent for the purchase of Italian built corvettes or light frigates.

item.title: MercoPress: British heritage in Chile, 1858 Catedral de San Pablo, refurbished in city-port Valparaiso
item.description: Chile's oldest Anglican church will be preserved as a museum to celebrate the role of the British Anglicans building religious tolerance in Chile. St Paul's Cathedral, (Catedral de San Pablo), brought together the early immigrant British community which settled in the central port city of Valparaíso, 120km away from the capital Santiago.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands commissions independent review (and survey) of the Tax system
item.description: The Falkland Islands Government has commissioned Alma Economics to undertake an independent review of the Falkland Islands tax system.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands at JMC: UK steps up security support for British Overseas Territories
item.description: The UK government and elected leaders and representatives from the Overseas Territories are meeting in London, beginning this Monday until November 26, for the annual Joint Ministerial Council (JMC). The JMC is a chance for UKOT leaders to come together to celebrate partnerships with UK and tackle the major challenges of our time.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Colombian police storm supermarket to free 20 held hostage for 17 hours
item.description: One gunman was killed in the operation to free around 20 shoppers and employees after a 17-hour hostage ordeal.

item.title: MercoPress: CIA and US intelligence office suffer intrusion exposing unclassified information
item.description: The Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and the US Office of the Director of National Intelligence recently discovered a computer intrusion that exposed unclassified information from an open-source intelligence analysis system, The New York Times reported on Tuesday. Unlike the system outages of recent weeks, attributed to technical failures, this is a security breach.

item.title: MercoPress: Argentina enters technical recession after two quarters of contraction, the first since 2024
item.description: Argentina's economy has entered a technical recession, with two consecutive quarters of contraction, for the first time since the first half of 2024. GDP fell 0.6% in the second quarter, and INDEC's monthly activity indicator points to a contraction of about 1.8% between July and September.

item.title: MercoPress: The flag at waist height: the rules for visiting the Argentine Military Cemetery in the Falklands
item.description: Tourism authorities in the Falklands have asked operators to remind visitors of the rules of conduct at the Argentine Military Cemetery at Darwin, while a programme to repair its stonework, which has deteriorated over time, is being drawn up. The rules, set out in a bilingual document, allow the Argentine flag to be placed on graves but consider holding it above waist height a political gesture.
item.category: Politics, Tourism, Argentina, Falkland Islands, International

item.title: MercoPress: Princess Anne visits South Georgia and sees British Antarctic Survey science at first hand
item.description: Princess Anne, the sister of King Charles III, visited South Georgia as part of her South Atlantic tour, meeting British Antarctic Survey scientists and staff stationed on the island, the Government of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands said on Monday. The visit to the islands, which began in the Falklands, was rejected by Argentina as a "provocation".
item.category: Health & Science, Politics, Antarctica, Falkland Islands, International

item.title: MercoPress: Argentina receives two bids for the Ushuaia naval base pier amid Sea Lion tensions
item.description: The Argentine government has received two bids to build the military pier at the Ushuaia integrated naval base, a project President Javier Milei relaunched in September, four days before the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea rules on Argentina's request to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands.

item.title: MercoPress: Colombia's peace deal turns ten with 36% of its commitments fulfilled
item.description: The peace agreement between the Colombian state and the former FARC guerrillas turns ten on Tuesday with only 36% of its commitments fulfilled, according to the Kroc Institute, more than 500 former fighters killed and a government that considers it a mistake.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Car bomb tears through Colombian city wounding more than 20
item.description: The explosion is the latest in a string of attacks on buildings housing the security forces and government offices.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Watch: Moment troops raid home and capture Mexican drug lord
item.description: Newly-released bodycam footage shows the moment troops detained 'El Chapo Isidro', who had managed to evade capture for years.

item.title: MercoPress: Pneumonia complicates Jair Bolsonaro's hospital stay in Brasília
item.description: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro has been diagnosed with pneumonia at the Brasília hospital where he has been admitted since Friday with an intestinal obstruction, his doctors said on Monday, although they ruled out surgery after his intestinal condition improved.

item.title: MercoPress: UK expresses support for Pedro Alliana's government in Paraguay
item.description: The United Kingdom has expressed its support for the government of Paraguayan President Pedro Alliana, who took office just over two weeks ago after the removal of Santiago Peña over the collapse of Ueno Bank, Paraguay's Foreign Ministry said on Monday.

item.title: MercoPress: Brazil's Supreme Court summons Flávio Bolsonaro by public notice over alleged slander of Lula
item.description: Brazilian Supreme Federal Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes on Monday ordered that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who is in the United States, be summoned by public notice to submit within 15 days his defence against a charge of slandering President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the state news agency Agência Brasil reported.

item.title: MercoPress: Brazil cuts its 2027 growth forecast to 1.8% and raises inflation to the top of its target
item.description: Brazil's Finance Ministry has cut its economic growth forecast for 2027 from 2.3% to 1.8% and raised its inflation forecast from 3.8% to 4.5%, the upper limit of the official target, according to its November Macrofiscal Bulletin. The government attributes the slowdown to high interest rates and more expensive credit.

item.title: MercoPress: Uruguay will not announce its CPTPP accession this year and will consult business and unions
item.description: Uruguay's Foreign Minister Mario Lubetkin has ruled out the government announcing before the end of the year the country's accession to the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), and said it will not move forward without consulting business and trade unions.

item.title: MercoPress: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after assurances from the US government
item.description: Nvidia's board on Monday reinstated founder Jensen Huang as chief executive and board member, weeks after his resignation, after receiving information from senior US government officials indicating that his return poses no risk to national security.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Mexican soldiers attacked in wake of drug lord's arrest
item.description: Eight suspects are arrested after firing on soldiers trying to re-establish order following the arrest of 'El Chapo Isidro'.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Seattle airport operator 'outraged' over ICE arrest of two Mexican passengers
item.description: ICE said a man and a woman, both Mexican nationals, were arrested for allegedly overstaying their visas.

item.title: MercoPress: Bolsonaro "clinically stable" in intensive care with an intestinal obstruction
item.description: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, in intensive care with an intestinal obstruction, is "clinically stable", the DF Star hospital in Brasília said on Sunday. Bolsonaro, 71, is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup, under house arrest.

item.title: MercoPress: COP31 ends without a major climate deal amid divisions over fossil fuels
item.description: The UN COP31 climate summit in the Turkish city of Antalya ended on Sunday without a major political agreement, after deep divisions between countries over fossil fuels and finance for the poorest. It is the first time since the 2009 Copenhagen summit that the main declaration of one of these conferences has collapsed in this way.

item.title: MercoPress: Colombia's government asks X to suspend Petro's account after he calls for the president to resign
item.description: The government of Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella asked the social network X on Sunday to suspend the account of former President Gustavo Petro, after he called on the public to demand the president's resignation.

item.title: MercoPress: Prosecutors: Argentina's top shrimp exporter dumped waste at sea through a hidden system
item.description: Two former managers of Conarpesa, Argentina's largest exporter of wild shrimp, have faced a new trial in Chubut province since this month over the discharge of fishing industry waste into the Golfo Nuevo, next to Puerto Madryn, through a hidden connection that prosecutors say the company set up.

item.title: MercoPress: Argentina's lawyer in Hamburg: if Sea Lion goes ahead, "those rights are lost forever"
item.description: Jurist Marcelo Kohen, one of the lawyers representing Argentina before the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea, has argued that if the United Kingdom begins extracting oil at the Sea Lion project north of the Falklands, Argentina's rights over those resources "are lost forever". The tribunal will announce on November 28 its decision on Argentina's request to suspend the project.
item.category: Energy & Oil, Politics, Argentina, Falkland Islands

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands: Public Accounts Committee to scrutinize several contracts and projects
item.description: The Falkland Islands Public Accounts Committee (PAC) announced this week, as part of its remit, its routine 2026/27 programme of oversight and scrutiny of a number of government projects and contracts.

item.title: MercoPress: Danstar to follow international maritime law: will seek clearance only for Punta Arenas departure and Stanley arrival
item.description: Pablo Pacheco, owner and general manager of the shipping company Easter Island Logistics, told the Chilean press that the cargo vessel Danstar "will strictly follow international maritime law" on its inaugural voyage between Punta Arenas and the Falklands, scheduled for December, which has prompted reports in Argentine media about an alleged request to cross Argentine waters.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
item.description: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores, who is accused of drug trafficking and torture, is detained after gun fight with authorities.

item.title: MercoPress: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro hospitalised in Brasília with abdominal pain
item.description: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, 71, was admitted to hospital in Brasília on Friday after suffering abdominal pain and distension, according to a statement from the medical centre where he remains. Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election, under house arrest on health grounds.

item.title: MercoPress: Trump threatens to penalise tech companies that build data centres outside the US
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Friday threatened to penalise American technology companies that build data centres abroad, through tariffs or other levies, although he did not explain what goal he was pursuing or how he would enforce the measure, and acknowledged he had not even presented the idea to his team.

item.title: MercoPress: UK and EU sign their biggest deal since Brexit in Brussels
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa signed three agreements in Brussels on Friday on food trade, carbon markets and youth mobility, the largest package agreed between the two sides since Britain left the European Union, a decade after the Brexit referendum.

item.title: MercoPress: Buenos Aires marks King Charles's birthday with a reconciliation message amid bilateral tension
item.description: The British Embassy in Buenos Aires celebrated King Charles III's 78th birthday on Thursday with a reception at which Ambassador David Cairns defended the strength of ties with Argentina despite "not-so-good days" and announced that in 2027 the 45th anniversary of the Falklands War will be marked together with veterans and families of the fallen from both countries.

item.title: MercoPress: Brazil's Central Bank sells US$1 billion to curb the dollar's rise
item.description: Brazil's Central Bank sold US$1 billion from its international reserves on Thursday in an attempt to curb the rise of the US currency, which approached 5.93 reais, amid financial market distrust of the fiscal adjustment proposed by Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government. The move brought initial relief, but the dollar rose again in the afternoon.

item.title: MercoPress: Colombia to euthanise hippos for the first time: ten animals in four months
item.description: Colombia's government will for the first time carry out chemical euthanasia on hippopotamuses, an invasive species in the country since drug lord Pablo Escobar brought the first animals to his estate in the 1980s. The Environment Ministry announced on Wednesday that ten animals in Antioquia department, located near populated areas, will be put down over the next four months.

item.title: MercoPress: Trump, Putin and Xi hold their first three-way summit, rich in symbolism but short on announcements
item.description: US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping held the first three-way meeting between the leaders of the three powers in Shenzhen on Thursday, an encounter rich in symbolism that ended with a commitment to dialogue on reducing nuclear risks but no concrete measures.

item.title: MercoPress: UK Parliament briefing details London's response to Argentina's offensive against Sea Lion
item.description: The House of Commons Library has published a research briefing setting out the response of Andy Burnham's government to Argentina's legal, economic and diplomatic offensive against the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands, nine days before the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea decides whether to order a halt.
item.category: Energy & Oil, Politics, Argentina, Falkland Islands, United States

item.title: MercoPress: Ueno Bank collapse claims Paraguay’s attorney general and the head of Itaipú
item.description: Paraguay’s Attorney General Emiliano Rolón resigned on Tuesday in the face of imminent impeachment, and the Paraguayan director of the binational Itaipú dam, Justo Zacarías Irún, was dismissed on Wednesday, in the latest wave of departures triggered by the collapse of Ueno Bank. At least a dozen senior officials have left their posts since the bank was taken over on November 3, among them President Santiago Peña, who was removed from office and is in prison.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Venezuela signs military deal with US less than a year after Maduro's ouster
item.description: The US Secretary of Defence says Venezuela has 'gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner'.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president
item.description: Christian Emmanuel Sanon is convicted of involvement in the plot that resulted in the killing of Jovenel Moïse.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Pope Leo rides in helicopter cockpit during Peru trip
item.description: The Pope took to the skies before arriving in Cusco on the penultimate day of his Latin America tour.

item.title: MercoPress: Gold's 10% decline in 2026 raises questions for global currency
item.description: A year ago, gold was the asset nobody could stop talking about. Its price rose more than 60% in 2025, the strongest calendar-year gain since 1979, and went on to set an intraday record near $5,600 an ounce in late January. By the end of October, however, the mood had soured, with spot gold touching about $3,870, roughly 10% below where it finished last year and more than 30% under that January peak.

item.title: MercoPress: IMF warns global debt will soon reach 100% of GDP, the highest since World War II
item.description: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned on Thursday that global public debt will soon reach 100% of world gross domestic product, the highest level since World War II, and called for "urgent attention" to government finances.

item.title: MercoPress: IMF’s Georgieva at APEC: countries must “quickly prepare” for artificial intelligence
item.description: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva on Thursday urged countries to “quickly prepare” their digital infrastructure, labour markets and workers for the rise of artificial intelligence, speaking at the plenary session of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.
item.category: Economy, Health & Science, Investments, Politics, International

item.title: MercoPress: US and Venezuela restore military cooperation with Hegseth’s surprise visit
item.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth signed a military cooperation agreement with Venezuela in Caracas on Wednesday during an unannounced visit, the first by a Pentagon chief since the January 3 US military operation that removed Nicolás Maduro from power. The agreement restores cooperation that Hugo Chávez broke off in 2005.

item.title: MercoPress: Anthropic, maker of Claude, debuts on Nasdaq after the largest IPO in history
item.description: US artificial intelligence company Anthropic, maker of the Claude assistant, begins trading on Nasdaq on Thursday after pricing its initial public offering at US$83 a share, above the expected range, in what the US financial press describes as the largest offering in history. The deal values the company at around US$1.5 trillion.

item.title: MercoPress: The smarter mobile matchday starts with better sports data habits
item.description: Across South America, following sport increasingly means moving between a live broadcast, a score alert, a group chat and a stream of statistics. A supporter in Buenos Aires may compare lineups before a Copa Libertadores match, while a fan in Bogotá follows a club abroad through a phone. The opportunity is obvious: more information, more access and more ways to understand a game. The challenge is knowing which numbers explain the contest and which simply demand attention.

item.title: MercoPress: Xi and Putin reaffirm their alliance on the eve of the first three-way summit with Trump
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin reaffirmed their strategic alliance in Shenzhen on Wednesday, hours before Xi personally greeted Donald Trump at the airport, on the eve of the first three-way meeting between the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States, to be held on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.

item.title: MercoPress: Hamburg tribunal confirms it will deliver its Sea Lion order on November 28
item.description: The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea has confirmed it will announce on Saturday, November 28, at noon Hamburg time — 8 a.m. in Montevideo and Buenos Aires — its decision on Argentina’s request for provisional measures to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands. The order will be read at a public sitting by the tribunal’s president, Judge Maurice Kamga.
item.category: Energy & Oil, Politics, Argentina, Falkland Islands, International

item.title: BBC Latin America: Venezuelan ex-world boxing champion Linares in ICE detention
item.description: Former three-weight world champion Jorge Linares remains in the custody of US immigration authorities in Texas and is facing deportation.

item.title: MercoPress: Argentina’s lower house debates Falklands sovereignty bill today, with one chapter short of votes
item.description: Argentina’s Chamber of Deputies debates the national sovereignty defence bill from noon on Wednesday, legislation that toughens sanctions for unauthorised resource exploitation in the Falklands. Javier Milei’s government is confident of passing it in general, but does not have the votes secured for the chapter on foreign interference, which requires a special majority.

item.title: MercoPress: Argentina calls Princess Anne’s visit to the Falklands a “provocation”
item.description: The Argentine government on Tuesday rejected the visit by Princess Anne, the sister of King Charles III, to the Falklands and South Georgia, calling it a “provocation” at a time when the United Kingdom, according to Buenos Aires, is advancing hydrocarbon exploitation in waters whose sovereignty Argentina claims. The Princess has been in the archipelago since November 9.

item.title: MercoPress: Microsoft, flights, banks and now the NSA: a week of tech outages in the US
item.description: The highly classified network the US National Security Agency (NSA) uses for its internal communications went down on Tuesday, the latest in a series of technology failures that in less than a week have hit Microsoft’s email, air traffic, online banking and Apple. No sign of a cyberattack has been found in any of the cases.

item.title: MercoPress: Sunday evening planning felt less rushed after a shift at the start
item.description: At 6:15 p.m., the dishwasher is humming and Monday's lunch is still undecided. I used to leave planning until I was already thinking about bed, which made even a short list feel like one more job.

item.title: MercoPress: Leo XIV after his tour: "There is no need to hate each other or use such violent language"
item.description: Pope Leo XIV criticised aggressive political debate and polarisation, "in many situations intentionally provoked", at the press conference he gave on his flight back to Rome after an eleven-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, in which he also said his health is good and recounted that he spoke with Argentine President Javier Milei about caring for those most in need.

item.title: MercoPress: Venezuela uses US$12 billion in US-supervised oil revenue to prop up the bolívar
item.description: Venezuela has spent most of the more than US$12 billion earned from oil sales under US supervision on propping up the bolívar, with modest results: inflation has slowed but remains the world's highest, and consumption has yet to recover.
item.category: Economy, Energy & Oil, United States, Venezuela

item.title: MercoPress: How Online Postgraduate Education Can Support South American Professionals in England
item.description: For South American professionals living in England, career development can involve adapting existing qualifications and experience to a different labour market. Someone who previously worked in finance, hospitality or management may encounter unfamiliar workplace expectations and recruitment requirements. Online postgraduate education offers an opportunity to develop advanced knowledge while continuing to work and build a professional future in England.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands close November with cricket, archery and hockey after opening Sports Complex
item.description: The Falklands are going through a month of intense international sporting activity, a week after the official opening of the new National Sports Complex in Stanley.
item.category: Investments, Politics, Falkland Islands, International, Latin America, Entertainment

item.title: MercoPress: FAO Food Price Index remained relatively stable during October
item.description: The benchmark measure of world food commodity prices edged lower in October, as weaker import demand contributed to month-on-month declines in the price indices for cereals, dairy products and meat, according to new data released by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO).

item.title: MercoPress: S.S. ‘United States’ Is Now the World’s Largest Artificial Reef
item.description: The World’s Fastest Ocean Liner finally hits the ocean floor. The 53,330-Ton S.S. ‘United States’ is now the world’s largest artificial reef. Longer than the “Titanic,” once carried celebrities and politicians across the Atlantic in midcentury style. Now, after decades of uncertainty and rust, it’s taking on a second life as an underwater refuge for marine creatures and curious divers, according to a piece from the Smithsonian Magazine.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Gunmen kill Costa Rican journalist who reported on drugs trade
item.description: Rodríguez had denounced alleged links between criminal organisations and powerful figures in Costa Rica.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Why Pope Leo’s visit 'home' to Peru is so significant
item.description: Pope Leo XIV celebrated a huge Mass for hundreds of thousands of pilgrims in Chiclayo, where he once served as bishop.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Millions fill Buenos Aires streets to welcome Pope Leo XIV
item.description: The Pope celebrated an outdoor Mass in Argentina's capital, the second stop on a 12-day tour of Latin America, just three weeks after having had surgery for lung cancer.

item.title: BBC Latin America: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton
item.description: Pasvill Lummer says children growing up in the 60s had a very different experience to their parents.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Pope Leo hit by flying rosary while waving to crowds in Peru
item.description: The pontiff was struck in the face by what is thought to be prayer beads while travelling aboard the popemobile to deliver a farewell Mass.

item.title: MercoPress: Orsi praises “excellent” ties with Milei and Lula’s re-election ahead of the Mercosur summit
item.description: Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi described his government’s relationship with Javier Milei’s administration in Argentina as “excellent” and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s re-election in Brazil as “fundamental”, in a Mercosur assessment given in Madrid less than three weeks before the bloc’s summit of heads of state in Montevideo on December 4.
item.category: Economy, Politics, Argentina, International, Mercosur, Uruguay

item.title: MercoPress: Venezuela accuses Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi of “interference” over call for free elections
item.description: Venezuela’s government on Monday rejected as “interference” remarks by Uruguayan President Yamandú Orsi, who had said hours earlier in Madrid that he cannot recognise a democratic government in Venezuela until free elections are held. Venezuelan Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco replied that the country’s future “belongs to the sovereign will of Venezuelans”.

item.title: MercoPress: British polar ship Sir David Attenborough sails from Montevideo for Antarctica
item.description: The British polar ship RRS Sir David Attenborough sailed from the port of Montevideo on Saturday bound for Signy Island in the South Orkneys to continue the British Antarctic Survey’s (BAS) 2026/27 Antarctic season, in a year in which the United Kingdom is without its military polar patrol ship, HMS Protector.
item.category: Environment, Health & Science, Antarctica, Falkland Islands, International, Uruguay

item.title: MercoPress: Milei’s government races to suspend primaries and pass the budget before year-end
item.description: Javier Milei’s Argentine government is accelerating a legislative agenda in the final weeks of the year whose priority is the suspension of the open primary elections, known as PASO, along with approval of the 2027 budget, reform of the Central Bank’s charter and the sovereignty defence bill, which toughens sanctions on companies operating in the Falklands without Argentine authorisation and has been cleared by committee in the Chamber of Deputies since late October.

item.title: MercoPress: Leo XIV denounces “market and exploitation logics” threatening the Amazon
item.description: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday denounced in Pucallpa, in the Peruvian Amazon, the “logics of market and exploitation” threatening the rainforest and its peoples, and demanded justice for Indigenous leaders killed for defending their territories, in the most combative speech of his visit to Peru, which ends on Monday.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Ashes of exiled Nobel Laureate Miguel Ángel Asturias returned to Guatemala
item.description: The poet, writer and diplomat died in Europe in 1974 having been forced to leave his native country.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Chapecoense air crash survivor wins promotion in final game
item.description: Alan Ruschel, one of six survivors in the 2016 plane crash that was carrying members of the Chapecoense team, wins promotion to Brazil‘s Serie A in his final match before retiring.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Vinícius Jr sends message to Sudan boy who received prosthetic legs after BBC report sparks appeal
item.description: Double amputee Zaher told the BBC last year about his favourite footballer and a dream of being able to walk again.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Mexican drug lord Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo dies age 80
item.description: Known as the 'Boss of Bosses', he was the head of all-powerful Guadalajara Cartel in the 1980s before his arrest broke up his drug organisation.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Wife of assassinated ex-Haitian leader registers for presidential election
item.description: There has not been an election in Haiti since before the death of Jovenel Moise in 2021.

item.title: MercoPress: Uruguay among the region’s most productive countries, but with below-average growth
item.description: Uruguay ranked fourth in Latin America and the Caribbean for labour productivity per hour worked in 2025, according to a report by the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC), but the indicator grew by only 0.6% during the year, below the regional average of 0.7%.

item.title: MercoPress: Leo XIV rides in a Peruvian military helicopter cockpit and reaches Cusco
item.description: Pope Leo XIV shared the cockpit with Peruvian Air Force pilots during one of his helicopter journeys on Saturday, in the final stretch of his South American tour, and on Sunday arrived in Cusco, the former capital of the Inca empire, the BBC reported.

item.title: MercoPress: Milei and Bullrich: a rift becoming routine ahead of the 2027 election
item.description: The tension between Argentine President Javier Milei and the ruling party’s Senate leader, Patricia Bullrich, has become part of daily life in La Libertad Avanza less than a year before the 2027 presidential election, and over the weekend it reached the international press. The British newspaper Financial Times devoted an analysis to the dispute on Saturday, citing a poll that ranks Bullrich as the most popular figure in the ruling camp.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands Post is releasing its newest South Georgia-Gentoo Penguin, November 18
item.description: The gentoo penguin (Pygoscelis papua) is one of South Georgia's most distinctive and widely distributed penguin species. Instantly recognizable by the broad white stripe that extends across the top of its head, together with its bright orange-red bill and pale pink feet, it is the world’s third-largest penguin species.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands: Princess Anne and community celebrate the opening of the spectacular Sports Complex
item.description: Princess Anne, sister of King Charles III, officially opened the Falklands’ spectacular new sports complex as part of the agenda for her visit to the South Atlantic islands, which will also include a sea passage to South Georgia.

item.title: MercoPress: Trump, Putin and Xi to hold their first three-way meeting in China on Thursday
item.description: US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold on Thursday, November 19, in the Chinese city of Shenzhen the first three-way meeting between the leaders of the three powers, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. Reducing nuclear arsenals and the war with Iran top the agenda.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Pope Leo rides in helicopter cockpit during Peru trip
item.description: The Pope took to the skies before arriving in Cusco on the penultimate day of his Latin America tour.

item.title: BBC Latin America: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is in Peru as part of his Latin America tour, just weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Ronaldinho makes comeback in Ravenna win
item.description: Brazil legend Ronaldinho makes his comeback aged 46 for Ravenna, playing the first half of their Italian third-tier derby against Forli.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Pope Leo speaks of community 'suffering' on visit to remote Andes town
item.description: Santa Cruz de Succhabamba is part of the Diocese of Chiclayo, where the pope served as bishop from 2015 to 2023.

item.title: MercoPress: US resumes flights after a four-and-a-half-hour shutdown caused by obsolete equipment
item.description: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on Friday night lifted the nationwide ground stop it had ordered in the afternoon, after some four and a half hours of airspace closure that left thousands of flights cancelled. Donald Trump’s administration blamed the failure on overloaded, outdated analogue telecommunications equipment at air traffic control centres, ruled out a cyberattack for now and warned that the return to normal would be slow.

item.title: MercoPress: British Antarctic Survey begins a season featuring the largest-ever penguin census
item.description: The British Antarctic Survey (BAS), the UK’s national operator in Antarctica, began its 2026/27 research season in late October, including the largest penguin census ever carried out on the continent, with flights from the British Rothera station and from Chile’s Marsh station on King George Island.

item.title: MercoPress: Un exbrigadista italiano se descuelga de un quinto piso en Buenos Aires para evitar su extradición
item.description: Leonardo Bertulazzi, a 74-year-old former member of Italy’s Red Brigades, escaped from house arrest in Buenos Aires on Tuesday by abseiling with a rope and harness from a fifth floor, after leaving his electronic ankle tag on a homemade device that simulated a human leg, to avoid imminent extradition to Italy. Argentine police on Friday arrested a Uruguayan man and a Salvadoran woman, identified as suspected accomplices, as they were about to cross into Uruguay.

item.title: MercoPress: US grounds all departing flights over an air traffic control communications failure
item.description: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on Friday ordered a halt to all flights departing from the country’s airports “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety”, following a communications failure affecting air traffic control centres. Thousands of flights were cancelled or delayed and hundreds of thousands of passengers were stranded. The government has so far ruled out an attack.

item.title: BBC Latin America: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is in Peru as part of his Latin America tour, just weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.

item.title: MercoPress: Microsoft restores services after a global outage hit Outlook and Teams in more than 70 countries
item.description: Microsoft said on Friday its services were recovering after a global outage that began on Thursday afternoon, European time, and for hours affected millions of users in more than 70 countries, including public bodies in Australia and Japan. The company ruled out a cyberattack.

item.title: MercoPress: Chile tells Argentina “countries do not ask permission” for its ship bound for the Falklands
item.description: Chile’s Foreign Minister Francisco Pérez Mackenna has ruled out asking Argentina for authorisation for the voyage of the Chilean vessel Danstar, which plans to reopen the commercial route between Punta Arenas and the Falklands in December, invoking the right of innocent passage recognised by the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. “Countries do not ask permission,” he said, according to Argentina’s La Nación.

item.title: MercoPress: Leo XIV to 52,000 young people in Lima: “Be passionate about everything worthwhile”
item.description: Pope Leo XIV met some 52,000 young people at Lima’s National Stadium on Thursday, according to El País, in the last event of his stay in the Peruvian capital before travelling to Chiclayo, the diocese he led as bishop. “Someone told me that Peru needs hope. You are the sign of hope,” he told them, to applause.

item.title: MercoPress: British veteran returns to an Argentine veteran the helmet he took in 1982
item.description: A former Royal Marine has travelled to Argentina to return to an Argentine veteran the helmet he took during the Battle of Mount Harriet in the 1982 Falklands War, in a reunion filmed for a documentary, BBC Sussex reported.

item.title: MercoPress: Lula to visit Madrid on Monday to meet Sánchez, two weeks before Spain’s election
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will visit Madrid on Monday, November 16, to meet Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, less than two weeks before the snap general election on November 29, in which Sánchez is seeking re-election. It will be Lula’s first visit to Spain since he won Brazil’s election on October 25.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Eight killed in Colombian air strike targeting Gulf Clan gang
item.description: A suspected gang leader considered a "priority target" was among those killed, the Colombian president says.

item.title: MercoPress: Paraguay’s banking superintendent arrested in the Ueno Bank investigation
item.description: Paraguay’s Superintendent of Banks, Holger Insfrán, was arrested on Thursday as part of the investigation into the collapse of Ueno Bank, which has already led to the pre-trial detention of former President Santiago Peña and former Central Bank president Carlos Carvallo, according to prosecution sources cited by the EFE news agency. The charges against him have not been disclosed.

item.title: MercoPress: Leo XIV arrives in Peru, his “homeland”, defending international law and reconciliation
item.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Lima on Wednesday, the final stage of his South American tour, and in his first speech in Peru, the country where he lived for some twenty years and whose nationality he holds, called for diplomacy that “respects international law” in the face of wars and for the country’s past events “to be dealt with justice and sensitivity”.

item.title: MercoPress: Aussie-Friendly Online Casinos: What the Account Actually Needs to Deliver
item.description: "Aussie-friendly" should describe practical account features, not a flag in the footer or a kangaroo in the artwork.

item.title: MercoPress: Law of the sea tribunal to rule on November 28 on Argentina’s bid to halt Sea Lion
item.description: The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea will announce on Saturday, November 28, its decision on Argentina’s request for provisional measures to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands, after two days of hearings concluded in Hamburg on Wednesday. Argentina presented final requests that were more specific than its initial ones, and the United Kingdom asked the tribunal to reject them all.

item.title: MercoPress: Milei in tears as he bids farewell to Leo XIV at Ezeiza, closing the Pope’s Argentina visit
item.description: President Javier Milei was moved to tears during Pope Leo XIV’s farewell at Ezeiza airport, at the end of a four-day visit, the first by a pontiff to Argentina in 39 years. The Pope left for Peru, the second leg of his South American tour, after celebrating his last Mass at the Basilica of Luján.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Kidnapper, 74, escapes from house arrest in Argentina by abseiling from balcony
item.description: Leonardo Bertulazzi, a former member of the Marxist guerrilla group the Red Brigades, was about to be extradited to his home country of Italy.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Transport workers in Chile block highways in protest over surging fuel prices
item.description: Hundreds of bus and lorry drivers are blocking traffic along major highway routes across the country.

item.title: MercoPress: Prosecutors open the vault at Peña’s house and find it empty; two safes found at Ueno Bank
item.description: Paraguayan prosecutors on Tuesday opened the armoured vault hidden in former President Santiago Peña’s summer house in San Bernardino, two days after finding it, and found it empty. In a second raid, at Ueno Bank’s headquarters, they found two more hidden safes, one containing about US$14,000 in cash.

item.title: MercoPress: EU-Mercosur deal, six months on: winners, losers and the question mark over Europe’s top court
item.description: Six months after it began to apply provisionally, the trade agreement between the European Union and Mercosur, made up of Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay, combines projected benefits for both blocs, opposition from part of Europe’s farming sector and a legal question mark: the opinion of the EU Court of Justice on its legality, which could take until early 2028.

item.title: MercoPress: Hundreds march in Gibraltar against Pelagos data center plan and demand transparency
item.description: This Saturday, there was a demonstration at Casemates Square organised to express public discontent with the endless construction projects in Gibraltar and the proposed mega data centre in particular.

item.title: MercoPress: Nvidia investigates founder Jensen Huang over his relationship with an alleged Chinese agent
item.description: Nvidia’s board has opened an independent investigation into founder and chief executive Jensen Huang after it emerged that he had an extramarital relationship with a businesswoman of Chinese origin whom US intelligence services link to Beijing’s espionage. President Donald Trump said on Monday that the FBI is investigating the case. No one has been charged.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Headquarters of Haitian gang destroyed, El Salvador's president says
item.description: The infamous 400 Mawozo gang was targeted by the El Salvador military which has deployed thousands of troops to combat Haiti's gang violence crisis.

item.title: MercoPress: Leo XIV draws some 650,000 to Córdoba with a homily on holiness
item.description: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass on Tuesday in Córdoba, in central Argentina, before some 650,000 people, according to the newspaper El País, in a homily devoted to holiness and local saints. “There is no better way to teach than by setting an example with one’s own life,” he told the faithful, urging them to practise their faith concretely in daily life.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
item.description: The ruling brings to an end an 11-year legal battle by dual-citizen Jason Jones.

item.title: MercoPress: Hamburg hearing opens as Argentina seeks to halt Sea Lion and the UK disputes jurisdiction
item.description: The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea began hearing Argentina and the United Kingdom in Hamburg on Tuesday over Argentina’s request for provisional measures to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands. Argentina argued that the resources of a disputed continental shelf cannot be exploited unilaterally, while the United Kingdom rejects the tribunal’s competence to rule on what it considers a question of sovereignty.
item.category: Energy & Oil, Politics, Argentina, Falkland Islands, International

item.title: MercoPress: Venezuela signs a memorandum with ExxonMobil for the oil major’s return after leaving in 2007
item.description: Venezuela on Monday signed a memorandum of understanding with US oil company ExxonMobil with a view to its return to the country, which it left in 2007 after the nationalisation of the last privately held oilfields under Hugo Chávez’s government. The document is not a contract, and no investment figures or timelines have been disclosed.º
item.category: Energy & Oil, Politics, International, United States, Venezuela

item.title: MercoPress: Nicaragua: Ortega reappears after 68 days as the government gives no word on his health
item.description: Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega reappeared in public on Monday night, 68 days after his last appearance, at a tribute in Managua to Carlos Fonseca, founder of the ruling Sandinista National Liberation Front. It was his longest absence since returning to power in 2007. The government has never reported on his health or explained his absences.

item.title: MercoPress: UK Defense minister admits Special Forces under mounting pressure and legal scrutiny
item.description: Britain’s Defense Secretary Wes Streeting has acknowledged the mounting pressures facing UK Special Forces (UKSF) amid ongoing legal scrutiny, as he attended his first Remembrance Sunday service since taking up the role.

item.title: MercoPress: Crash Games Explained: Why This Simple Format Became So Popular
item.description: A line climbs across the screen, a number beside it ticks up from 1.00x, and at some unknown moment the line stops, and the round is over. Anyone who cashed out before that moment wins their stake multiplied by the number on screen, and anyone still in loses everything they bet. Few casino games can be explained in two sentences, and that simplicity goes a long way toward explaining how crash became one of the most played formats in online gaming.

item.title: MercoPress: Princess Anne and Sports VIPs present at official opening of Falkland Islands Sport Complex
item.description: The Falkland Islands Government and National Sports Council are proud to announce the official opening of the Falkland Islands’ new National Sports Complex, this Tuesday 10 November, in the presence of HRH The Princess Royal and Vice Admiral Sir Tim Laurence.

item.title: MercoPress: UK with eyes from space: launches its second military satellite, Titania
item.description: Britain has a new pair of eyes in space, with the successful launch of British-built military satellite Titania. The launch – completed last month from California on an Space X rocket– will further help the Armed Forces coordinate their efforts on and above Earth, by improving their ability to observe military activity on Earth from space.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands Sports Complex, the joint effort of Government and private sector companies
item.description: The opening of the new multi-sports Falkland Islands National Sports Complex makes the Islands’ community reflect on the joint effort that brought this to fruition.

item.title: MercoPress: RN inaugurates “hybrid navy” with its First Autonomous Squadron of un-crewed boats
item.description: The Royal Navy has created a squadron made up of un-crewed boats for the first time in its efforts to move towards a 'hybrid navy'. The 28ft boats will be based at Portsmouth Naval Base and will be dedicated to operating autonomous boats on the front line.

item.title: MercoPress: Princess Anne arrives in the Falklands and will open the new National Sports Complex
item.description: Princess Anne, the sister of King Charles III, arrived in the Falklands on Monday with her husband, Vice Admiral Sir Tim Laurence, at the start of a visit that will later take her to South Georgia, and among other engagements will formally open the new National Sports Complex in Stanley.

item.title: MercoPress: Some 2.5 million people attend Leo XIV’s Mass in Buenos Aires, authorities say
item.description: Some 2.5 million people, according to local authorities, attended the Mass Pope Leo XIV celebrated on Monday in the parks of Palermo in Buenos Aires, the first by a pontiff in Argentina since John Paul II’s visit in 1987, with a homily focused on the role of the family. El País described it as the largest gathering of his pontificate.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Millions fill Buenos Aires streets to welcome Pope Leo XIV
item.description: The Pope celebrated an outdoor Mass in Argentina's capital, the second stop on a 12-day tour of Latin America, just three weeks after having had surgery for lung cancer.

item.title: MercoPress: The first Islander aircraft built entirely in the UK arrives in the Falklands
item.description: The Falkland Islands Government Air Service (FIGAS) is welcoming a new Islander aircraft on Monday, VP-FTS, the first of the type to be assembled entirely in the United Kingdom, which arrives in Stanley from Punta Arenas, Chile, after a delivery flight of almost three weeks.

item.title: MercoPress: Hidden armoured vault found in a Peña home built with Ueno Bank loans
item.description: Paraguayan prosecutors and police on Sunday searched a residence of former President Santiago Peña in Ciervo Cuá, in the San Bernardino district, about 50 kilometres from Asunción, built with loans from Ueno Bank. According to the newspapers ABC Color and Última Hora, they found an armoured vault behind a false wall that they were unable to open. The Prosecutor’s Office confirmed the search, although its statement did not mention the vault, whose contents are unknown.

item.title: MercoPress: 1982 veterans parade in London as the Falklands honour the fallen on Remembrance Sunday
item.description: The Falkland Islands community paid tribute on Sunday in Stanley to those who lost their lives in conflict at the Remembrance Sunday service, while in London many British veterans of the 1982 war paraded at the main commemorations.

item.title: BBC Latin America: King relishes 'politically charged' deployments, Palace aide says
item.description: The monarch faced questions on the UK's involvement in the slave trade during his Caribbean tour.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Pope delivers veiled rebuke of Milei's austerity measures
item.description: Pope Leo made the comments as he arrived in Argentina on the second leg of his Latin America tour.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
item.description: Pope Leo travels to Uruguay just three weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.

item.title: MercoPress: Lost savings and broken trust: life for those hit by Ueno Bank’s closure
item.description: For nearly three million Paraguayans, November 3 began with a message on their phone screens: “We cannot display your balance.” Early that morning, Paraguay’s Central Bank took over Ueno Bank over a critical solvency problem and froze its deposits. A week later, with President Santiago Peña removed from office and in pre-trial detention, many of those affected still have no access to their money and say they have also lost faith in the country’s institutions.

item.title: MercoPress: Leo XIV, before Milei: “The economy must serve the person”
item.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Buenos Aires on Sunday, the first papal visit to Argentina in 39 years, and in his first address to the authorities, with President Javier Milei at his side, said that “the economy must be at the service of the person, and not the person at the service of the economy”, urged those in authority to “recognise the limits of power” and called for “special attention” to the sick and people with disabilities.

item.title: MercoPress: Leo XIV leaves Uruguay urging Catholics to reach out to “those who have drifted away”
item.description: Pope Leo XIV ended his visit to Uruguay on Sunday with a Mass before some 30,000 faithful in the city of Florida, where he urged Catholics to reach out to those who have drifted away from the Church in South America’s most secular country, before flying to Buenos Aires, the second stop on his regional tour.

item.title: MercoPress: Paraguay’s prosecutors charge Santiago Peña and seek his pre-trial detention over the Ueno Bank collapse
item.description: Paraguayan prosecutors on Saturday charged former President Santiago Peña, removed from office by the Senate on Friday, and requested his pre-trial detention in the case over the collapse of Ueno Bank, which froze the savings of nearly three million customers. A judge must rule on the request. Prosecutors also charged former Central Bank president Carlos Carvallo, who is in custody.
